title: George Duvivier's running jokes
summary: He and Duvivier pretend to hate each other, including a spat about driving Duvivier's Cadillac.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: That's right. You take George Du- vivier, now. He's another one of my worst enemies. We used to walk in the studio, and if we see one another first -- somebody first, -- he'd holler out, "Who's playing drums?" And somebody would say, "Gus Johnson." "Gus Johnson? Give me my bass, let me get the hell out of here."
If I know he's there and I see him, I say, "Oh, no, no, I can't play with him. Get somebody else, I don't make the gig, just like that. And everybody's looking, "What's wrong
with him? Looky at there, he can't play with him? As good a bass player as George Davivier? " And we still carry on like that.

And we passed through Denver, I'm driving his car, see. We stop downtown for a light, and we're just arguing. He's arguing about my driving his car. So I told him, "Just get the hell out of my car, just like that. His Cadillac, he gets out and slams the door. "Well, just take your old car and get out of here, " and I'd just drive right on off and leave him on the corner and go around the corner, and he's standing there.

I say, "Hey, buddy, what do you know?" He'd say, "Hey." I'd say, "You want a ride?" He'd say, "I don't care if I do." And he'd get in the car and everybody's looking and saying, "What's wrong with him?"
